newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyed as transit point for defector - official.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyed as transit point for defector - official.

text.p: The Philippines has been asked to serve as a transit point for a senior North Korean defector in Beijing if he is allowed to leave for South Korea, Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Saturday.
Siazon told reporters the request was made by both South Korea and China and he strongly indicated the Philippines was prepared to agree to the request.

"There are talks going on based on the request of the Republic of Korea and also China to find a way of having this gentleman go to his destination without going through a straight route, and we have been asked," Siazon said.

"Our view is if the three countries concerned are informed and we are being asked to find a solution, then in order to make our contribution to resolving this problem - because we are all in Asia - we don't wish this particular problem to evolve into a more serious politicial difficulty among the three parties, so we would in that context be prepared to make our contribution."
Siazon spoke to reporters before he left for an official visit to Japan.

Hwang Jang-yop, a North Korean ideologue and top aide to supreme leader Kim Jong-il, has been stranded at the South Korean consular compound in Beijing since February 12. He is the most senior official to defect from North Korea and talks have been taking place between the two Koreas and China on his fate.
